newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court issues arrest warrants for unionists.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court issues arrest warrants for unionists.

text.p: A South Korean court on Friday issued arrest warrants for seven leaders of a militant union body spearheading nationwide strikes, a prosecution official said.
Earlier, Kwon Young-kil, president of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions and six deputies rebuffed police trying to deliver a summons for them to appear in court.
Kwon has threatened all-out stoppages, including a public sector shutdown, if arrests are carried out.
Police investigators supported by several hundred riot police burst into confederation headquarters shortly before midnight on Thursday to seize documents.

State prosecutors had asked for the arrest of the seven on charges of obstructing business by staging illegal strikes. The judge first said he wanted to question them but issued the warrants after they rejected the summonses.
